mission.brief: Locate and read web.conf in configuration storage, web.log in log storage, and todo.txt in your home. List the log directory and finish in /home/learner. Learn explains each location. Grading checks successful inspection at the correct paths, not a verbal explanation of their purposes.
constraints: Read-only virtual filesystem. No file-management mutations in this introductory lab.
Successful cat at each required file and ls of /var/log are action evidence; current directory is a final-state objective. Equivalent supported paths/order count.
Use help, pwd, ls [-l] [PATH], cd [PATH], cat PATH only. No shell expansion, scripts or host actions.

objectives.label: Final state: finish in your home

hints: Use ls to inspect likely directories before reading a file. The location matters, not just the filename.
Configuration commonly belongs under /etc; changing logs under /var/log; your work under your home. This small tree is a preparation exercise, not a full FHS assessment.
Read /etc/web.conf, list /var/log and read /var/log/web.log, then read /home/learner/todo.txt and finish in /home/learner.

/var/log/web.log.content:
2026-10-03 web: training page loaded
# /var/log stores changing log data.

/home/learner/todo.txt.content:
Prepare a workspace and organize the handover.
# Your home stores your own work.

lesson.goal: Locate configuration, log and personal files, read them, then finish in your home.

steps.explanation: System-wide configuration commonly lives in /etc. Read this small simulated setting.
Logs are changing data; /var/log is a common location. List the directory to find the file.
Read the log entry at its actual location. This is a simulated text log, not a journal query.
A home directory holds personal working files. Read your task note.
steps.expected: Prepare a workspace and organize the handover.

steps.explanation: Return to your own working directory. The rubric checks where you finish.
